book.title: Daily Mail New Cryptic Crosswords, volume 2

clue.text: Come in and sit by the fire!

definitions.text: Come in and sit by the fire!

parts.words: Come in and sit by the fire!
parts.note: surface reading: a host asking a cold visitor indoors
setter's reading: the whole invitation is the friendly greeting itself, the kind a guest is glad of

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is the host's actual words; the answer names what those words amount to, with the fire adding the warmth.
explanation.definitionFit: An invitation indoors to the fireside is a cordial, hospitable reception, literally and figuratively heated.

clue.text: Reason taking pounds might be convincing

definitions.text: Reason taking pounds might be convincing

parts.words: Reason taking pounds might be convincing
parts.note: surface reading: a logical case that persuades
setter's reading: pounds are units of weight, so a reason that has put on pounds is a heavy one

explanation.surface: A sound reason, perhaps one involving money, is persuasive.
explanation.walkthrough: Pounds suggests money, but here it is weight: a case carrying weight is a strong, persuasive one.
explanation.definitionFit: A forceful, serious case in debate is called weighty, so a persuasive line of reasoning fits exactly.

clue.text: Member of dock family talking nonsense

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a stalked plant in the same botanical family as the dock weed
second meaning: meaningless chatter, as actors murmur in crowd scenes

explanation.surface: Someone from a family of dockers is spouting rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Dock suggests a harbour; it is the broad-leaved weed, a relative of the garden plant whose stalks are stewed.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant belongs to the knotweed family alongside docks, and the word is also slang for empty, babbling talk.

clue.text: Finish showing how the others can get a take-away

definitions.note: noun in the surface; the answer is the verb 'take away'

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its final letter, so only the end of the next word is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of this word
the rest are the others, the remainder

explanation.surface: Seems to explain how a group's leftovers can be turned into a takeaway meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Take-away looks like a meal; it is the verb. Finish is not the definition but an instruction applied to the word after showing.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrest something is to pull or seize it away from someone by force, a forcible taking.

clue.text: Creature taken in by an amorous couple not eaten

definitions.note: adjectival phrase; the answer is a noun for food not eaten

indicators.note: being taken in by something means being held inside it

parts.note: a romantic pair
an eft is a newt, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A pair of lovers too busy to eat take in a small animal.
explanation.walkthrough: Amorous couple pulls toward romance, but it simply supplies the outer word; the newt is the small creature held inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Food remaining on the plate after a meal, uneaten, is what we call the remains of dinner.

clue.text: Is ape to get fuddled by drugs?

indicators.note: fuddled means muddled or confused, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters as printed

explanation.surface: Asks whether a monkey is going to be befuddled by narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: Opiates are narcotics derived from opium, such as morphine and codeine, so they are drugs.

clue.text: Giving birth on a train ensures a quick arrival

definitions.meaning: first meaning, whimsically: a childbirth (delivery) aboard a fast train (express)
second meaning: a fast postal or courier service

explanation.surface: A baby born aboard a train arrives in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a playful literal reading of the two words; the second is the ordinary postal service.
explanation.definitionFit: The postal service of that name promises speedy dispatch, so a parcel sent by it arrives quickly.

clue.text: Artist in trouble finds a restricted way through

indicators.note: something in trouble is in disorder, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter in difficulty discovers a narrow escape route.
explanation.definitionFit: A strait is a narrow channel of sea between two land masses, a confined passage for ships.

clue.text: Time spent here isn't free

parts.note: surface reading: a place where you pay for your stay
setter's reading: time is a sentence served, and the inmate is literally not free

explanation.walkthrough: Free seems to mean costless; it means at liberty, and time is a jail term.
explanation.definitionFit: Inmates serve a sentence of time locked up in a jail, deprived of liberty.

clue.text: Platform for speaker finding support in the air

indicators.note: one item sits within the other here

parts.note: an air is a melody
a rib supports a structure such as a vault or boat

explanation.surface: An orator's stage gets propped up in mid-air.
explanation.walkthrough: The air is a melody, not the sky; the support is a structural strut, as in a boat's frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribune is a raised dais or rostrum from which an orator addresses an assembly.

clue.text: Aviator accepting twopence to aid swimmer

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so one part is held within the other

parts.note: one who flies
two pennies, each abbreviated P

explanation.surface: A pilot takes a small coin to help someone swimming.
explanation.walkthrough: PP goes inside FLIER after FLI. P is the abbreviation for a British penny.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber fin worn on the foot is a swimming accessory, propelling divers through water.

clue.text: Drunkard loses the place and comes back still a drinker

indicators.note: coming back means travelling the other way, so what is left reads backwards
losing something means dropping it, so part of the word is taken out

parts.note: an old word for a habitual boozer
a spot is a place

explanation.surface: A drunk is thrown out of the pub yet returns, still drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: Tosspot is an old word for a boozer. Still here just means nevertheless and gives nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A sot is a habitual heavy boozer, someone who drinks to excess.

clue.text: What strange pictures when seen sideways!

indicators.note: strange means odd or out of the ordinary, so the preceding word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
paintings and pictures are art

explanation.surface: An exclamation at how odd paintings look when viewed from the side.
explanation.definitionFit: Athwart means across or transversely, from side to side, so crosswise or at an angle.

clue.text: Markets means of escape

definitions.meaning: first meaning: places or channels where goods are sold
second meaning: vents or exits that let something out

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like markets offer a way out; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Retail shops and sales channels are commercial outlets, and pipes or vents that release water or gas are outlets too.

clue.text: Go for what's not finally fashionable

indicators.note: read as 'not fin-ally': without its end, a word meaning end being taken from inside

parts.note: trendy means in fashion

explanation.surface: Pick what is slightly out of date.
explanation.walkthrough: Not finally is a pun: 'not END'. TRENDY with END removed leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A go is an attempt, as in 'have a go', which is the same as having a shot.

clue.text: Tucker's associate left with no measure giving ultimate authority

parts.note: from the phrase 'bib and tucker', one's best clothes

indicators.note: having no part of something means that part is removed

parts.note: taken as written
FT is the abbreviation for foot, a measure of length

explanation.surface: Sounds like a sidekick of someone named Tucker was given the final say.
explanation.walkthrough: A tucker was a lace piece worn at the neck; 'best bib and tucker' means one's finest clothes. LEFT loses FT to leave LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Scripture, or any book treated as definitive, is the supreme source consulted and obeyed without question.

clue.text: Wish happiness to embrace dear rogue with no sign of ageing

indicators.note: an embrace wraps around, so one part goes inside the other

parts.note: to bless is to wish someone joy

indicators.note: a rogue thing behaves erratically, so the letters next to it are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone congratulates a youthful rascal with a hug.
explanation.walkthrough: Rogue looks like a noun for the rascal; it is the signal to rearrange the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth, unbearded chin marks youth, since growing whiskers comes with maturity.

clue.text: Giving her a black eye might be a bloomer

definitions.text: Giving her a black eye might be a bloomer

parts.words: Giving her a black eye might be a bloomer
parts.note: surface reading: punching a woman would be a big mistake
setter's reading: a bloomer is a flower, and adding black-eyed to a woman's name gives a daisy-like plant

explanation.walkthrough: Bloomer seems to mean blunder; it is something that blooms. Black-eyed Susan is a yellow flower with a dark centre.
explanation.definitionFit: The girl's name, preceded by black-eyed, is the common name of the rudbeckia flower.

clue.text: It's sung in a beautifully rich voice

indicators.note: the letters wanted are sitting inside the words that follow

parts.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second
surface padding that completes the singing picture

explanation.surface: A song performed by a singer with a lovely full voice.
explanation.walkthrough: Voice completes the picture of singing and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyrics are the words of a song, the text a singer performs.

clue.text: Strikes over the eyes

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the hairs fringing the eyelids

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as blows to the face, but the second half is the hairs on the eyelids.
explanation.definitionFit: A lash is a whipstroke, and eyelashes are the short hairs growing along the eyelid rims.

clue.text: Accommodation a bit too much in confinement

indicators.note: one piece placed within another

parts.note: a cage confines
OTT stands for over the top, rather excessive

explanation.surface: Being locked up seems rather excessive as lodging.
explanation.walkthrough: Confinement could mean childbirth; here it is something that confines. OTT is a British abbreviation for over the top.
explanation.definitionFit: A small country house is a dwelling, a place to live in, so it is housing.

clue.text: It's worth having a girl back

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: going back means running the other way, so the name is read from its end

parts.note: a girl's name

explanation.surface: Having a girlfriend return is worthwhile.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is something valuable that one owns, a useful possession.

clue.text: What we have here is let out to represent people in the North

definitions.text: to represent people in the North
definitions.note: infinitive phrase for the emblem that represents them

parts.note: this is what is here

indicators.note: out means disordered or wrong, so the letters before it are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something here is being rented out to stand for northerners.
explanation.walkthrough: Let out suggests renting; out is the anagram signal. The North here means Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The prickly purple plant is Scotland's national emblem, standing for the Scots.

clue.text: Show bitterness leaving the old craft for a long time

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so those letters go away from the word

parts.note: a sailing ship of past centuries
gall is bitterness or rancour

explanation.surface: Someone resentful spends ages away from traditional handicrafts.
explanation.walkthrough: Craft looks like skill; it is a vessel. GALLEON minus GALL leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An eon is an immeasurably vast period, an age, so it is an extremely lengthy duration.

clue.text: One's sense of what's right is taking off

definitions.text: One's sense of what's right is taking off

parts.words: One's sense of what's right is taking off
parts.note: surface reading: someone's morality is soaring, as a plane takes off
setter's reading: taking off clothes, a creed whose followers believe it right to go bare

explanation.walkthrough: Taking off seems to mean rising sharply; it means undressing, and the creed is the belief that being unclothed is right.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturism is a belief and practice holding that going about unclothed is proper and healthy.

clue.text: Gave showy performances not allowed proper growth

definitions.meaning: second meaning: held back from developing fully

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase it sounds like a child actor kept small; they are two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Stunts are daring tricks, and a plant or child whose development is checked is described as dwarfed or stunted.

clue.text: Made one take a turn if due in

indicators.note: taking a turn means twisting about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters as printed

explanation.surface: Someone is told to have a go if they are expected to arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: To unify is to merge separate parts into a single whole, so joined together.

clue.text: Superior meal not needing a starter

indicators.note: a starter is the opening, so the first letter is dropped

parts.note: an evening meal

explanation.surface: A fine dinner that skips the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: Starter looks like a first course; it is the first letter of the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Higher in rank or position, as in the upper classes, means superior.

clue.text: One might take some stick for looking brighter

definitions.text: One might take some stick for looking brighter

parts.words: One might take some stick for looking brighter
parts.note: surface reading: someone teased for appearing cleverer
setter's reading: a cosmetic stick applied to a part of the mouth makes it more vivid

explanation.walkthrough: Taking stick usually means being criticised; here it is the stick of colour applied to the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Lipstick is applied to the mouth's edge, which therefore takes stick to look more colourful.

clue.text: Put up girl to replace one in high society

indicators.note: replacing means swapping in for something, so one letter is taken out and another piece put in its place

parts.note: the elite are the top people
the Roman numeral for one
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is promoted to stand in for someone among the upper classes.
explanation.walkthrough: In ELITE the I is swapped for EVA.
explanation.definitionFit: To elevate something is to raise or lift it higher, which is to hoist it.

clue.text: Messes about when swimmers are quiet

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
otters are swimming animals

explanation.surface: Someone fools around while bathers are silent.
explanation.walkthrough: The quiet P comes first, though the clue names it last.
explanation.definitionFit: To potter is to busy oneself idly with small tasks, pottering about aimlessly.

clue.text: Urge seer to move in attempt at controlling growth

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a try is an attempt

indicators.note: moving the letters about rearranges them

parts.note: the letters as printed

explanation.surface: Someone urges a prophet to try to restrain a spreading crop.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled letters sit inside TRY after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Arborists prune and lop limbs of woody plants to manage their size and shape.
